## Module 5 in two minutes

> ⚠️ **Counsel review required before deployment.** Every specific here moves and must be confirmed for your own jurisdictions.

**A course can be pedagogically excellent, factually accurate, well-reviewed — and non-compliant, inaccessible, or built on something you do not own.** Every quality signal your function uses would return clean on all four. Same structure as premise inheritance: your checks are aimed at a different layer than the risk.

**Mandated content is specified, and the specification is not about quality** `[V]`. Statutes name duration, interactivity, and content elements. A generated course omitting a required element is non-compliant and the audit gives no partial credit. **The requirement is an input, not a review criterion.**

**Deferral is not runway** `[V]`. EU high-risk employment duties moved to 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 — but AI literacy and the absolute workplace emotion-recognition ban have bound since February 2025, and the transparency obligations since 2 August 2026. A learning chatbot must disclose it is AI, whatever its risk class.

**Accessibility exposure scales with asset count** `[V]`, and concentrates in the cheap-to-produce bucket nobody reviewed. Uncaptioned video arrives by default.

## The rule

**A skills inference becomes a decision about a person the moment an allocation of opportunity depends on it.**

The tell is not what the system outputs — it is what happens downstream of the output. Nobody experiences building a taxonomy as building a decision engine, which is why 101 M7's line has never been pointed here.

## What the full module adds

The specific state mandates and why multi-state means strictest-applicable or genuinely separate versions. Why the emotion-recognition prohibition matters to *this* function specifically — engagement-scoring-from-video is marketed here. The five predictable ways AI-generated media fails WCAG 2.1 AA, and why the fix is cheap at production time and a project afterwards. The three questions that resolve whether an inference is a decision, and the boundary with the People Analytics specialism: **they own whether the inference is any good; you own what happens to a person because of it.** The four ownership questions. Ten uses to sort. And the activity: three real assets sampled, one mandate compared element by element, and the line written down.
